name: Front Struts, Springs & Top Mounts
description: Front MacPherson strut assemblies: damper (MRC on ZL1, Multimatic DSSV on ZL1 1LE/SS 1LE, conventional on SS), coil spring, spring seats/insulators, top mount, and race alternatives (coilovers, camber/caster plates, helper springs). The strut clamps to the knuckle with two torque-angle bolts and bolts to the tower with three bolts.

components.name: Front strut / damper
components.description: Load-bearing MacPherson strut that locates the top of the knuckle and provides front damping. Factory ZL1 uses monotube Magnetic Ride Control struts; ZL1 1LE uses Multimatic DSSV spool-valve struts with aluminum bodies and a threaded spring seat for ride height/corner-weight adjustment. Race builds use double- or triple-adjustable coilover struts with remote reservoirs, matched to the chosen spring rate.
components.location: Between the knuckle upper clamp (approx x 0.01, y 0.50, z +/-0.665) and the strut tower top (x 0.05, y 0.85, z +/-0.55).

factory.name: ZL1: Magnetic Ride Control monotube strut; ZL1 1LE: Multimatic DSSV aluminum-body strut (RPO FEA)
factory.notes: 1LE DSSV top mounts are hard mounted (no rubber isolation). SS non-MRC cars use conventional struts; the GM SG3 sport-suspension kit (84408106) fits 1SS/2SS non-MRC and LS/LT. Struts are side-specific (LH/RH). A brake hose bracket and wheel-speed-sensor harness retainer attach to the strut body.

raceOptions.name: Multimatic DSSV (factory ZL1 1LE) retained
raceOptions.notes: Excellent non-adjustable baseline; revalve possible through specialists. Threaded perch gives +/-10 mm ride height.

raceOptions.name: Öhlins Road & Track / TTX-style coilover
raceOptions.notes: Check current Gen 6 Camaro application; pair with BMR WAK361 or similar plates.

raceOptions.name: KW Variant 3 / Clubsport coilover
raceOptions.notes: Gen 6 Camaro kits exist (verify part number for MRC vs non-MRC cars).

raceOptions.name: Custom double/triple-adjustable strut (Penske, JRi, MCS)
raceOptions.notes: Built to order on Gen 6 strut geometry (knuckle clamp, tower mount); best for dedicated race car with remote reservoirs.

specs.Type: MacPherson strut, double-pivot lower (two ball joints)
specs.ZL1 1LE spring seat adjustment: approx +/-0.4 in (10 mm); approx 0.06 in (1.5 mm) ride height per turn
specs.Lower clamp: 2 bolts + nuts to knuckle (21 mm bolt head / 24 mm nut per BMR instructions)

hardware.item: Front suspension strut bolt + nut (strut-to-knuckle clamp)
hardware.spec: Large flange bolt and nut, 21 mm head / 24 mm nut (thread size not published; approx M14-M16)
hardware.torqueSequence: First pass 150 N·m (111 lb ft), final pass +80-95 deg
hardware.notes: Per strut. Support the knuckle while inserting bolts. GM SG3 instructions.

hardware.item: Front brake hose bracket bolt at strut
Wheel speed sensor harness retainer (push-in clip to strut bracket)

installNotes: Assemble the strut (spring, seats, insulators, top mount) on the bench with a proper strut spring compressor (GM CH-45400-A or equivalent).
Position strut in tower; install the 3 upper mounting bolts loosely.
Install the two strut-to-knuckle bolts (support the knuckle); torque nuts 150 N·m + 80-95 deg.
Install sway bar link nut (100 N·m) and then torque the 3 upper bolts to 22 N·m.
Install brake hose bracket (10 N·m) and WSS harness retainer; check hose and sensor wire for slack at full lock and full droop/bump.
inspection: Check for oil weeping at rod seal and reservoir hoses.
Check strut clamp bolt witness marks.
Verify damper adjuster settings are recorded on setup sheet.

components.name: Front coil spring
components.description: Coil spring concentric with the strut, seated between the lower spring seat on the strut body and the upper spring seat under the top mount. Race cars replace the progressive OE spring with a linear race spring (typically 2.5 in / 60-65 mm ID on coilovers) sized for target ride frequency, plus an optional helper/tender spring to keep the main spring seated at full droop.
components.location: Around the upper strut, center approx x 0.035, y 0.70, z +/-0.60.

factory.name: GM front coil spring (rate varies by RPO: FE2/FE3/FE4/FEA)
factory.notes: Factory rates are not published by GM; GM SG3 kit lowers approx 20 mm on non-MRC cars.

raceOptions.name: Hyperco / Swift / Eibach ERS linear race spring (2.5 in ID)
raceOptions.notes: Typical Gen 6 road-race front coilover rates approx 600-1000 lb/in (estimate; non-aero to moderate aero). Choose by target front ride frequency approx 2.0-2.8 Hz.

raceOptions.name: BMR SP041 lowering springs (performance)
raceOptions.notes: Street/track lowering spring set for OE dampers.

specs.Front motion ratio (strut): approx 0.9-1.0 (strut nearly in line with wheel; estimate)

installNotes: Spring tag/paint mark orientation per manufacturer; ensure coil ends seat in insulator stops.
Record free length, rate and part number on the setup sheet; spring-rate test new springs.
inspection: Check spring seating and coil bind clearance at full bump.

components.name: Front strut top mount (strut mount / bearing) and rod nut
components.description: The top mount bolts to the strut tower with three bolts and holds the damper rod through a rubber isolator (ZL1/SS) or hard mount (ZL1 1LE DSSV). On the 1LE the mount can be rotated 180 deg from the street to the track position for additional negative camber. The damper rod nut is torqued with a hand tool (GM warns against impact guns on rod nuts).
components.location: Strut tower top, x approx 0.05, y approx 0.85, z +/-0.55.

factory.name: GM front strut mount, mount washer and rod nut (with cap)
factory.notes: Stack order (top to bottom): strut mount nut, strut mount, strut mount washer (small diameter up against mount, large against upper seat), upper spring seat, upper insulator, spring.

hardware.item: Front suspension strut mount nut (damper rod nut)
hardware.spec: Rod nut (18 mm hex per BMR); use GM CH-50732 socket or equivalent rod-hold socket
hardware.torqueSequence: Spring compressed; hold rod; torque by hand tool
hardware.tool: CH-50732 or 18 mm rod-nut socket with hex hold
hardware.notes: 60 N·m per GM SG3 kit (non-MRC). Some GM SI listings: 50 N·m with RPO F55 (MRC) / 65 N·m without - use the value for your damper. No impact guns.

hardware.item: Strut upper mounting bolt (mount to tower)
hardware.notes: Tighten after strut-to-knuckle bolts are torqued.

installNotes: On ZL1 1LE choose street or track (rotated 180 deg) mount position before final torque, then align.
Never use an impact gun on the rod nut (rod damage/breakage per GM).
inspection: Re-torque tower bolts after first outing.

components.name: Threaded spring perch / height-adjust collar
components.description: Threaded lower spring seat on ZL1 1LE DSSV struts and on all race coilovers. Adjusts ride height and corner weight without changing spring preload rate. On the 1LE: approx +/-10 mm range, approx 1.5 mm height per full turn; do not let the seat contact the black dust boot at the top of travel.
components.location: On strut body below the spring, approx y 0.58-0.62.

factory.name: ZL1 1LE (RPO FEA) threaded spring seat
factory.notes: Not on ZL1 MRC or SS struts.

raceOptions.name: Coilover threaded sleeve + lock collar
raceOptions.notes: Use spanner wrenches; lock collars after corner weighting.

specs.1LE adjustment: +/-0.4 in (10 mm), 0.06 in (1.5 mm) per turn

installNotes: Set approximate ride height on the bench (measure perch-to-mount), refine on scales at phase 11.
inspection: Check lock collar tightness after every session early on.

components.name: Front camber/caster plate (race top mount)
components.description: Replaces the factory top mount with a spherical bearing mount that slides in slots for camber and caster adjustment. Essential for road-race front camber (-3 deg and beyond) and to equalize caster side-to-side, since factory caster is not adjustable.
components.location: Strut tower top, x approx 0.05, y approx 0.86, z +/-0.55.

factory.name: N/A (ZL1 1LE has a rotatable street/track mount instead)

raceOptions.name: BMR WAK360 caster/camber plates (factory spring)
raceOptions.notes: 3/16 in CNC laser-cut steel, Teflon-lined spherical bearing, approx 2.5 deg total camber range plus caster adjustment.

hardware.item: Plate-to-tower bolts (through aluminum spacer bracket and nut plate)
hardware.spec: Supplied bolts with washers (long set for use with BMR strut-tower brace, short set without)
Button head socket cap screw (7/16 in hex key)

hardware.item: Caster slider to camber plate bolts
hardware.spec: Socket head cap screw (1/4 in hex key)

hardware.item: Damper rod nut onto caster slider
hardware.torque: 37 ft-lb (50 N·m) for MRC/F55 damper rods; 44–48 ft-lb (60–65 N·m) for non-F55 rods
hardware.notes: Use GM rod nut value; hold rod, no impact. [2026-10 check] GM values differ by damper. The 1LE kit sheet (F55/MRC strut) gives 50 N·m. The 2016 SG3 sheet 84188729 (non-F55) gives 65 N·m, and the 2017 SG3 sheet 84408106 gives 60 N·m. TightTorque: 50 N·m with F55, 65 N·m without. GM gives no value for ZL1 1LE DSSV dampers, and BMR WAK360 gives none, so use the damper maker's rod-nut spec when one exists.
hardware.torqueSequence: Hold the rod with a rod-nut socket (CH-50732, 18 mm). Hand tools only: GM warns that impact drivers can break the rod.

installNotes: Offset hole in the camber plate goes toward the REAR of the car (BMR).
Set initial camber/caster to the target alignment numbers using slot positions, then align.
inspection: Mark slider position with paint pen; check for slip after each session.

components.name: Helper / tender spring and coupler
components.description: Short, very soft spring stacked above or below the main race spring with a spring coupler. It keeps the main spring captive at full droop (inside wheel lifting) without adding preload, which is common with stiff race springs on a strut car.
components.location: On the coilover above the main spring.

raceOptions.name: Hyperco / Swift / Eibach helper spring + coupler
raceOptions.notes: Match ID to main spring (2.5 in typical).

installNotes: Helper should be fully coil-bound at static ride height.
